subject: ss-paediatric-radiology
title: Duodenal Atresia, Malrotation and Midgut Volvulus

steps.say: Duodenal atresia produces the classic double-bubble sign on plain abdominal radiographs. Complete absence of distal bowel gas is characteristic, and thirty percent of infants have Down syndrome.
steps.tx: Recognize the **double-bubble sign** of duodenal atresia on neonatal plain abdominal radiographs. Congenital duodenal atresia results from failure of recanalization of the embryonic duodenum. Plain radiographs demonstrate two prominent gas collections representing the dilated stomach and duodenal bulb, with complete absence of distal bowel gas; 30% have Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) (Normal DJ flexure anatomical position).

vis.alt: Bowel constricted by an adhesion band with air fluid levels on film.
vis.caption: Obstruction: dilated bowel with air fluid levels. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The upper gastrointestinal series is the definitive gold standard for diagnosing malrotation. Look carefully for a displaced duodenojejunal flexure that fails to cross the midline.
steps.tx: Establish the **normal DJ flexure anatomical position** on upper gastrointestinal fluoroscopy. On AP and lateral fluoroscopic views, the normal duodenojejunal (DJ) flexure lies to the left of the left pedicle of the vertebral column at or above the level of the duodenal bulb. In intestinal malrotation, the DJ flexure is displaced inferiorly and to the right of the spine, failing to cross the midline (Corkscrew sign of volvulus).

left.title: Normal DJ flexure
points: Located left of left vertebral pedicle
Positioned at or above duodenal bulb level

right.title: Malrotation DJ flexure
points: Displaced inferiorly and to the right
Fails to cross the spinal midline

steps.say: When volvulus supervenes on malrotation, contrast outlines a spiraling, twisted duodenum. This corkscrew appearance is pathognomonic of acute midgut volvulus.
steps.tx: Identify the **corkscrew sign of volvulus** during an emergency upper gastrointestinal contrast study. When the malrotated midgut twists clockwise around its narrow vascular pedicle, contrast injected into the stomach traverses the pylorus into a dilated proximal duodenum, which then spirals downward in a tight helical twist resembling a corkscrew, heralding immediate operative intervention (Ultrasound whirlpool sign).

vis.alt: Dilated proximal bowel, strangulation and radiographic air fluid levels.
vis.caption: Volvulus risks strangulation of dilated bowel. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates the whirlpool sign, confirming midgut volvulus. Swirling of the superior mesenteric vein and mesentery around the superior mesenteric artery is diagnostic.
steps.tx: Demonstrate the **ultrasound whirlpool sign** at the patient bedside. Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrates the whirlpool sign: clockwise spiraling of the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and mesentery around the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). This real-time bedside finding confirms midgut volvulus and vascular strangulation, prompting emergency surgical consultation without waiting for fluoroscopy (Reversed SMA-SMV relationship).

rows: SMV located to the right of SMA
SMV positioned anterior or to left of SMA
Fails to pass between aorta and SMA

steps.say: Under normal conditions, the superior mesenteric vein runs to the right of the artery. Reversal of this relationship, with the vein to the left or anterior, strongly indicates intestinal malrotation.
steps.tx: Evaluate for a **reversed SMA-SMV relationship** on transverse abdominal ultrasound. Under normal anatomical conditions, the superior mesenteric vein lies to the right of the superior mesenteric artery. Reversal with the SMV located to the left or directly anterior to the SMA strongly indicates intestinal malrotation, reflecting developmental non-rotation of the fetal mesenteric root (Ladd bands pathology).

left.title: Normal mesenteric anatomy
points: SMV located to the right of the SMA
Third duodenum passes between aorta and SMA

right.title: Reversed SMA-SMV anatomy
points: SMV located to the left or anterior to SMA

steps.say: Ladd bands are abnormal peritoneal fibrous bands that fix the malrotated cecum to the right abdominal wall. These bands compress the descending duodenum, causing mechanical obstruction.
steps.tx: Understand the **Ladd bands pathology** causing extrinsic duodenal compression. In malrotation, congenital peritoneal fibrous bands (Ladd bands) fix the abnormally positioned cecum in the right upper quadrant to the right posterior abdominal wall. These dense fibrous bands cross directly over the descending and transverse duodenum, causing extrinsic mechanical obstruction even in the absence of acute midgut volvulus (Duodenal web windsock sign).

nodes.label: Cecum positioned in right upper quadrant
Ladd bands form across descending duodenum

steps.say: An intraluminal duodenal web results from incomplete recanalization of the embryonic gut. Contrast series provide clear demonstration of the windsock sign, where a thin membrane stretches distally into the lumen.
steps.tx: Identify the **duodenal web windsock sign** during upper gastrointestinal fluoroscopy. Incomplete duodenal recanalization produces an intraluminal duodenal web with the windsock sign: a thin mucosal membrane stretching distally into the second or third duodenum on contrast series, outlined by contrast on both its proximal and distal surfaces with a small eccentric pinhole aperture (Jejunal and ileal atresia triples).

left.title: Duodenal web (windsock)
points: Outlined by contrast on both sides

right.title: Extrinsic duodenal stenosis
points: Caused by annular pancreas or Ladd bands

steps.say: A triple bubble sign indicates jejunal atresia caused by an in utero vascular accident. Distal ileal atresia shows multiple dilated loops with air-fluid levels and a microcolon.
steps.tx: Recognize **jejunal and ileal atresia triples** on neonatal abdominal radiographs. A triple bubble sign indicates jejunal atresia caused by an intrauterine vascular mesenteric accident; distal ileal atresia shows multiple dilated loops with air-fluid levels and a unused microcolon on barium enema, differentiating high proximal jejunal atresias from distal ileal obstructions.

rows: Triple bubble sign; few distal bubbles
Multiple dilated loops with air-fluid levels
